unit: RT-B: fishing_room, egg_room, fossil_chamber (docs/mechanics/DUNGEON_PASS2.md 'Next phase'; docs/research/notes/dungeon-room-mechanisms.md sections 1-3)
why: Three optional rooms that tell whole dungeons apart. Every number marked DESIGN is the balance designer's to tune; nothing here is run in Minecraft (experiments/EXP-089-dungeon-fish-egg-fossil).

fishing.why: A vibey pool with better chances for cool species, starters among them (the owner). Mechanism: a boxed spawn_pool_world entry (dimension cobblers:pocket, the dungeon's four slot rows) keyed to a BAND MARKER block hidden under the pool, not a Habitat Block. Why: (1) a spawn entry cannot see the entrant's band, and the pool must differ by band (levels at or under the band's lower cap so the level-cap catch block never refuses; stage of the line by band), so the slot reset writes the entrant's marker and each entry requires it in neededNearbyBlocks (a FishingSpawningCondition field, read from the 1.8.0 jar); (2) a Habitat Block is a block entity that a command-placed shell activates only after a chunk reload (EXP-021) and whose fishing influence has never been tested; a datapack entry has neither problem. Every stock fishing entry (591, scanned in the jar) needs a biome, a structure or a dimension the void pocket has not, so only these entries fire. The wanted species sit in the common bucket (83% of rolls, server best-spawner-config) because a species in 'rare' is rolled 4% of the time whatever its weight; each band still carries one species in every bucket so no rolled bucket is empty.

pool.why: 9 x 7 water, one deep (the walk check's wading depth: a deeper pool is a pit). 9 keeps every bobber within 4 blocks of the centre marker (neededNearbyBlocks looks at a 10-block cube round the bobber)

markers.why: one block per band, three cells in the pool bed under the pier. None is used by any theme or by the puzzles' marks (data/dungeon_puzzles.json uses red, blue, yellow, lime, purple, orange).

decor.why: water cells away from the pier

rod.name: Lent Rod
rod.why: The player's own rod is not assumed: the room lends one (a plain Poke Rod marked cobblers_lent_rod) at the first step in. It is taken back wherever the engine takes the rift pick back (a run's end, the far rip, the back rip: tools/dungeon_extras2.py patch_functions adds one line after each `clear @s <pick>`), and by the slot reset. A player who keeps their own rod simply has two.

fishing.level_rule: lo = max(5, lower cap - 10), hi = lower cap of the band (data/dungeons.json engine.bands caps[0]): never above what the cap lets the entrant catch

item_catches.unit: dungeon fishing, 2026-10-17 (the owner, after casting in the Flooded Ruin's cast_pool: 'i got a tripwire hook, i think the pool for fishing in dungeons needs to be only hits, to make it worth it. so enchant books, gold, pokemon, pokeballs, etc')
item_catches.why: A Poke Rod bite is a Pokemon with probability pokemonSpawnChance (85 by default), else an ITEM from the loot table cobblemon:fishing/pokerod (Cobblemon 1.8.0 and 1.8.2 jars: identical): junk 66 / pokerod_treasure 17 / vanilla treasure 17, both treasure entries gated on the bobber being in OPEN water, which a one-deep pool is not, so a dungeon cast's item was junk, a tripwire hook. tools/dungeon_extras2.py emits that table again at the same path (data/cobblemon/loot_table/fishing/pokerod.json, a deliberate override of an upstream path: nothing in the build or the COBBLEVERSE datapacks overrides it today) with one new entry first: when the loot context's ORIGIN (the bobber) is in the pocket dimension (vanilla minecraft:location_check, predicate.dimension, 1.21.1 loot-table condition) it rolls the dungeon table below and nothing else; the upstream entries each gain the inverse of that test, so anywhere else the pool is exactly the upstream pool (weights, quality, conditions untouched). A loot context carries no scoreboard and no band (origin, tool, luck, the bobber), so the table is one table for every band, sized to the middle of the catch values rather than the top.
item_catches.value_why: cp is a hundredth of a point and a point is $100 (data/dungeon_greed.json). Pokemon caught on the same rod weigh 100 to 200 cp by band (catches.cp_by_band) and are CHARGED to the clock; an item catch is not charged (GREED measures mined blocks, opened chests and caught Pokemon only, not a fished item), so it is held to about one catch: the table's expected value per ITEM bite is in range_cp, and 15% of bites are items, so an item adds about a third of a point per bite. The vault's chests are worth up to dollar_factor 2.0 times the gathering tier (data/dungeon_greed.json vault_budget), well above one bite. NOTHING here sells to the bank (data/bank.json buys minerals; gold_ingot and gold_nugget are not in buys; raw gold is deliberately not given) and none is a Produce Buyer specimen, so a cast cannot turn into cash.

left_out.cobblemon:fishing/pokerod_treasure: the owner asked for Cobblemon's own fishing treasure. Four of its five items (deep_sea_scale, deep_sea_tooth, dragon_scale, prism_scale) are Produce Buyer specimens that sell for cash (data/produce_buyer.json specimens.items), so a dungeon source would be a cash route that the buyer's 'drop only' safety property rules out; kings_rock is the fifth and is not a specimen, so it is given on its own. Outside the pocket they are still rolled as before, in open water.

the jackpot: an Ultra Ball ($800), one bite in a hundred of the items
the owner's gold; the bank does not buy ingots (bank_removed at 22)

an enchanted book, vanilla's own fishing-treasure form (minecraft:gameplay/fishing/treasure: a book enchanted at 30 levels from #minecraft:on_random_loot). Priced by proxy at the fossil chamber's greed_cp (300: 'three of the owner's diamonds'): nothing prices a book
the one non-sellable item of pokerod_treasure; a held item no recipe makes, priced by proxy at two fossils

eggs.why: A vendor (a non-battling NPC) sells one egg a run. The egg is given with Cobbreeding's `givepokemonegg` (the 2.3.0 jar registers the literal and its `player` and `properties` arguments; permission command.cobbreeding.egg.give at the cheat level), run as the player from a function: an egg cannot be written with /give (its species is an encrypted component). It hatches in the player's inventory while they walk (about ten minutes at the default multiplier, ASSUMED), so a forty-minute run hatches it.

price.why: PRICE IS CLOCK TIME, not CobbleDollars and not an item. (1) The engine's own currency is the run's clock (a vault chest costs clock_cost_s; a fall costs fall_penalty_s), so no new sink needs an arbitrage audit. (2) CobbleDollars cannot be priced against the game from here: the dungeon takes money back from every NPC win (the clawback), a dollar price would have to be re-balanced against the gathering tiers per band, and `cobbledollars remove` takes min(amount, balance) so it needs a query first and fails open. (3) An item price would make the room need a currency item the player carried in, so a player with an empty bag meets a vendor they cannot use. (4) The numbers: a small trainer fight is 120 + 30 x (members - 2) seconds (tools/dungeon_clock.py fight_s), so an egg, a Pokemon you did not fight for, costs about one small fight, 90-150 s by band. DESIGN numbers. The sale is refused when fewer than min_left_s remain after the price, so buying can never end the run.
price.greed_why: A taken egg is a Pokemon taken, so it weighs on the clock as a nest catch for the entrant's band (data/dungeon_greed.json catches.cp_by_band.nest: 1 to 2 points), through greed/add like a catch. Every valuable taken counts (tools/dungeon_greed.py).

fossils.why: Dig for a fossil. NO brushing: the Wiki's adventure table lists brushing as impossible and every item's use-on-block needs can_place_on (NeoForge ItemStack patch), so the dig is the rift pick's: a bay of dig blocks with ONE fossil block hidden in the middle layer (rolled at the first step in from 8 spots), breakable under the pick's can_break exactly as the resources room's seam is. Mining the fossil block is counted by GREED's minecraft.mined stat; the room's tick sees the cell turn to air and gives the fossil from a loot table by band. Dust drifts from the wall in front of the hidden block so the dig has a place to start.

bay.why: 7 wide counting a frame column each side, so 5 x 3 x 3 = 45 dig cells, against the north wall (the seam's slab depth): the frame and a lintel of the theme's wall block close it, so no one-wide nook forms. The fossil is rolled among 8 of the 15 middle-layer cells.

fossils.particle_why: emitted in the air in front of the face above the fossil: a particle inside a block is hidden by the block's face
fossils.greed_why: DESIGN number: 3 points (+0.15x), three of the owner's diamonds. 14 of the 15 fossils have no other source (docs/research/OBTAINABILITY_VANILLA_COBBLEMON.md) and a restored fossil is a Pokemon, which a catch weighs 1 to 2 points; one block per run, so the room can weigh at most 3 points
